HealpixDenseChunkSettings.description:
Chunk output data along the HEALPix cell dimension according to
HEALPix cells given at a parent, "coarse" refinement level (dense version).

Each of those "chunk" cells are densely populated with adjacent children
HEALPix cells all at the same "fine" refinement level.

Chunk size is thus fixed and is given by the following formula:

.. math:: 4^{(\Delta - \delta)}

where :math:`\Delta` is the parent level (output chunks) and :math:`\delta` is
the child level (output data values).

This chunking strategy works only with the "nested" HEALPIX cell indexing scheme.
HealpixDenseChunkSettings.title: HealpixDenseChunkSettings

healpix_coordinate_codecs.description:
Zarr codecs of the HEALPix cell ids coordinate (zarr's defaults if None).

The cell ids of a chunk are sorted, and one contiguous range with
``healpix_cell_dense`` chunks, which zstd alone keeps at about one byte per
cell. A delta filter before the compressor brings them to almost nothing,
e.g. ``[{"name": "numcodecs.delta", "configuration": {"dtype": "<u8"}},
{"name": "bytes"}, {"name": "zstd"}]``; readers then need an implementation
of that codec. The delta filter is meant for plain cell ids: with
``healpix.compression`` set to ``"compacted"`` or ``"ranges"`` the ids are
already compressed and it brings no further gain.
healpix_coordinate_codecs.title: Healpix Coordinate Codecs

codecs.description:
Zarr codecs of the group's resampled data variables (other arrays use
zarr's defaults).

Each codec is looked up by name in zarr's codec registry, so the package
that provides it must be installed where the settings are created, e.g.
``healpix-compress`` for ``hcc-sentinel2-pyramid``.
codecs.title: Codecs

HealpixGroupSettings.title: HealpixGroupSettings

HealpixSparseChunkSettings.description:
Chunk output data along the HEALPix cell dimension according to
HEALPix cells given at a parent, "coarse" refinement level (sparse version).

Each of those "chunk" cells are populated with sparsely distributed children
HEALPix cells given at a "fine" refinement level.

Chunk size is user defined. There's no strict constraint on the minimum
size, which should be large enough such that a parent "chunk" cell can
contain all output data values (children cells). If all children cells are
at the same refinement level, the maximum size is given by the following
formula:

.. math:: 4^{(\Delta - \delta)}

where :math:`\Delta` is the parent level (output chunks) and :math:`\delta` is
the child level (output data values).

This chunking strategy works only with the "nested" HEALPIX cell indexing scheme.
HealpixSparseChunkSettings.title: HealpixSparseChunkSettings

exclude_attrs.description:
Names of the input dataset attributes that must not be propagated to the output.

Each item is either the exact name of an attribute or a regular expression
matched against the whole attribute name (e.g., ``"history.*"`` excludes both
``"history"`` and ``"history_of_appended_files"``).
exclude_attrs.title: Exclude Attrs

override_attrs.description:
Attributes set on the output variables, overriding the input ones.

Each key is either the exact name of a variable or a regular expression
matched against the whole name (e.g., ``"b0[1-9]|b8a"``), and each value the
attributes set on the matching variables.

An override wins over ``exclude_attrs``, and the last of several matching
patterns wins. The attributes written by healpix-convert itself
(``grid_mapping``, ``coordinates``) keep precedence.
override_attrs.title: Override Attrs

PyramidSettings.description:
Settings for generating a pyramid of coarser HEALPix refinement levels
in a multiscale group.

The derived levels given by :py:attr:`derived_levels` are aggregated from
the levels converted from the input data (the native levels of the
multiscale group).

The derived levels are written in the multiscale group, next to the native
levels or in a child group of its own (see :py:attr:`subgroup_name`).

Every child group of the multiscale group must be converted with the
``healpix_cell_dense`` chunk method: the cells of such a chunk are all the
children of one HEALPix cell, which is what lets the derived levels be
aggregated by position (see
:py:func:`~healpix_convert.generate_pyramids`).

derived_levels.description:
HEALPix refinement levels to derive, e.g. ``[18, 16]``.

Each of them must be coarser than the finest native level of the multiscale
group and must not be one of its native levels (which are converted from
the input data).
derived_levels.title: Derived Levels

subgroup_name.description:
Name of a new group, direct child of the multiscale group, where the
derived levels are written, e.g. "pyramids"::

    reflectance          (multiscale group)
    ├── 20               (native level)
    ├── 19               (native level)
    ├── 17               (native level)
    └── pyramids
        ├── 18           (derived level)
        └── 16           (derived level)

If None (default), the derived levels are written next to the native
levels, as direct children of the multiscale group::

    reflectance          (multiscale group)
    ├── 20               (native level)
    ├── 19               (native level)
    ├── 18               (derived level)
    ├── 17               (native level)
    └── 16               (derived level)

Either way the multiscale group holds every level of the pyramid, and its
multiscales metadata describes them all.
subgroup_name.title: Subgroup Name

reduce.description:
How the values of the children cells are aggregated.

Missing (NaN) values are skipped. The mean does not suit categorical data
(masks, classifications): aggregate those with "mode", the most frequent
value of the cells of a block (the smallest of them in case of a tie).
reduce.title: Reduce

coarsen_from.description:
Which native level a variable converted at several levels is aggregated
from: the nearest level at or finer than the derived level (default),
i.e., the copies resampled by the data provider are kept and reused, or
always its finest native level, i.e., those copies are ignored.
coarsen_from.title: Coarsen From

STACSettings.description:
Settings for the STAC metadata (``stac_discovery``) written in the root
group of the output dataset.

include_conversion_settings.description:
If True (the default), the conversion settings are recorded in the output
as the ``processing:expression`` STAC property.

Set it to False to leave them out, e.g., because they are large or because
they name internal paths that should not be published. The rest of the
provenance (``processing:datetime``, ``processing:software``,
``processing:lineage``) is written either way.
include_conversion_settings.title: Include Conversion Settings

merge_properties.description:
How the STAC properties of several input datasets are merged.

``"join_inner"`` keeps the properties every input has with the same value,
i.e., what they agree on: a ``datetime`` that differs across the inputs
does not describe the output either.

With a single input dataset both strategies are equivalent.
merge_properties.title: Merge Properties

merge_extensions.description:
How the STAC extensions of several input datasets are merged.

``"join_outer"`` lists every extension any input declares, which is what
keeps the output item from dropping a namespace its properties still use.
merge_extensions.title: Merge Extensions

merge_links.description:
How the STAC links of several input datasets are merged.

Links have no identifier, so they are merged whole: two links are the same
one when they are equal. ``"join_inner"`` keeps the links every input has
and ``"join_outer"`` every link any input has, in the order they first
appear.
merge_links.title: Merge Links

merge_assets.description:
How the STAC assets of several input datasets are merged.

Merged like the properties, by asset key. The result is then filtered by
``exclude_assets``, which drops every input asset by default.
merge_assets.title: Merge Assets

exclude_properties.description:
Names of the input STAC properties that must not be propagated to the output.

Each item is either the exact name of a property or a regular expression
matched against the whole property name (e.g., ``"internal:.*"`` excludes
every property of an ``internal`` namespace).

The properties written by healpix-convert itself (``processing:*``) keep
precedence.
exclude_properties.title: Exclude Properties

override_properties.description:
STAC properties set in the output, overriding the propagated ones.

An override wins over ``exclude_properties``. The properties written by
healpix-convert itself (``processing:*``) keep precedence.
override_properties.title: Override Properties

exclude_extensions.description:
Input STAC extensions that must not be listed in the output.

Each item is either the exact URL of an extension schema or a regular
expression matched against the whole URL (e.g.,
``"https://stac-extensions.github.io/projection/.*"`` excludes any version
of the projection extension).

The STAC processing extension, listed by healpix-convert itself, keeps
precedence.
exclude_extensions.title: Exclude Extensions

override_extensions.description:
URLs of the STAC extension schemas listed in the output, in addition to
the propagated ones.

An override wins over ``exclude_extensions``.
override_extensions.title: Override Extensions

exclude_links.description:
Input STAC links that must not be propagated to the output.

Links have no identifier, so each item is matched against the whole ``rel``
of a link: either an exact relation type (e.g., ``"via"``) or a regular
expression (e.g., ``"self|parent|root"``).

The ``derived_from`` links written by healpix-convert itself keep
precedence.
exclude_links.title: Exclude Links

override_links.description:
STAC links written in the output, in addition to the propagated ones.

Each item is a whole link object (``rel``, ``href``, and whatever else the
link carries). An override wins over ``exclude_links``.
override_links.title: Override Links

exclude_assets.description:
Keys of the input STAC assets that must not be propagated to the output.

Each item is either the exact key of an asset or a regular expression
matched against the whole key (e.g., ``"thumbnail.*"``).

Every input asset is excluded by default: the assets of the input point at
the input files, which the output does not hold, so propagating them would
have the output item advertise files that are not its own. Set this to an
empty list to keep them, or describe the output's own files with
``override_assets``.
exclude_assets.title: Exclude Assets

override_assets.description:
STAC assets set in the output, overriding the propagated ones.

Each key is the key of an asset and each value the whole asset object
(``href``, ``type``, ``roles``, etc.). An override wins over
``exclude_assets``.
override_assets.title: Override Assets
